_note: DECLARED subject renumbers. Copy to docs/ledger-renumbers.json and declare your own.
_why: The sequence predicate compares subjects as EXACT STRINGS and normalises nothing, deliberately: guessing at intent is how a gate starts agreeing with its author. A BOARD MIGRATION breaks that premise honestly -- an item's `intake` and `claim` carry the number it had when it was FILED while its `close` carries the number it has NOW -- so the close is refused for legs that exist three inches away under the old number. A declared map is the repair; the three derivations (arithmetic, reading the live number-map at gate time, fuzzy subject matching) were each refused on measurement. See resolved_sequence_problems in tools/ledger.py.
_rules: Each entry maps the subject a row carries NOW to the subject it carried WHEN IT WAS FILED.
`was` and `evidence` are both required and both non-blank: a renumber names the subject it was AND the receipt that establishes the step.
A resolution only FINDS legs that already exist under the declared prior subject. It never manufactures one: an entry whose `was` carries no legs changes nothing and the close is still refused.
Positional semantics are preserved -- the prior subject's legs must still precede the close's own index.
Chains are followed (this factory's board was migrated twice), bounded at 8 hops with a visited set.
Every resolution is PRINTED with its evidence on every pass, and the count is printed at zero too, so 'none resolved' and 'the map was not consulted' cannot read alike.
ABSENT means none. A factory that has never renumbered a board has nothing to declare.
